_provenance: Per-capability scores as supplied by the owner on 2026-08-12 (the format and the current state, given together). AGENTS.md's locked baseline after MEM-005 was Nexeo 45.3 vs professional 92; these numbers are the later state and supersede it. Capability ORDER is BRAIN_VISION.md's and must not be reordered (AGENTS.md, required audit sequence step 1).
_rules: Evidence-based capability judgements, NOT test-pass percentages. Every score change must name the iteration and the evidence that moved it. Green tests alone never raise a score. Anything unexercised or unfalsifiable in production is UNVERIFIED and does not raise it either.

history.head: 518475e
history.evidence: Owner-supplied post-build scorecard carried forward as the baseline for the loop's reporting.

history.head: 087c54b
evidence: Accurate Communication +1: DEF-135 (1940a34) — B12 recovered 0 -> 95 on the real composer path; the guard stopped destroying the answer around a real fabrication, and the fabricated process claim no longer reaches the user. Held to +1, not more, because Codex's HIGH finding shows the salvage still ships an unverified CAUSE (fabricated-status shape) and the post-build judge independently flagged it (C1=85 on B12).

history.head: 545a69a
evidence: No capability moved. DEF-136 (9cf416d) built the shared prose-finalisation chokepoint, and Codex verified it SOUND with no unsupported claims — the first build log to survive scrutiny intact. But C4 rose only 85.4 -> 86.3 and Codex's own attribution says why: 'DEF-134's unreachable guard was real but low-impact in this benchmark.' Closing a bypass without moving a capability is worth 0 here, not +1.

Codex also flagged a MEDIUM risk introduced by the change: the form normaliser is unanchored, so a reasoning answer quoting 'Hamna wrote: "Hi Basit Ahmed, ..."' would have the QUOTE rewritten to 'Hi Sir, ...' — Brain misquoting evidence. That is a reason not to credit the iteration, not a reason to debit it, since it is unshipped.

history.head: fb3f36b
evidence: Accurate Communication +1: DEF-137/138 (e428a2d) — the persona said address was optional 'one reply in four' while four of its eight EXAMPLES addressed the user (50%, double the stated ceiling); examples outvote prose in a prompt. C4 rose 86.3 -> 89.6, its largest move, B05 reached 95, and Codex verified SOUND after re-running tsc/1947 tests/build/diff itself. Held to +1: verified on the COMPOSE surface only, and CL-033 shows the same address rule does not reach the proactive notification path, where a live message addressed the owner as 'Basit,' instead of the configured form.

history.head: 52729be
history.verdict: NEUTRAL (Codex WEAK — right mechanism, incomplete coverage, live-unverified)
evidence: Accurate Communication +0: DEF-140 (ede14fa) removed a genuine SECOND address resolver — brainHumanComm.addressUser read user.name's first token while brainPersonaService honoured the configured 'Sir', which is why a live draft ask said 'Basit,'. Codex confirmed the diagnosis and called the composition-first deviation CORRECT. No credit yet, for two stated reasons: (1) Codex raised two HIGH findings — provenance is OPTIONAL and only 7 of ~66 inventoried producers are classified, and notificationService.ts:122-141 sends owner WhatsApp content without entering the boundary at all, so an unclassified producer can still ship 'Basit,' with nothing failing; (2) it is live-unverified — Codex: 'remains locally verified and live-unverified until an actual proactive draft/chase message uses Sir rather than Basit.' The compose benchmark bought no evidence either way, which Codex judged as scope discipline rather than uselessness.

history.head: 72e7a02
evidence: Accurate Communication +0: DEF-143 (aef1540) caught a fabricated developer-remediation clause the previous iteration's detector missed, and Codex granted that plus 'useful register guidance'. But verdict WEAK on two counts that block credit: its salvage test DECLARES the adjacent unverified reminder-cause claim TRUE, preserving the baseline's most serious C1/C2 defect, and it widened a block-and-excise regex with known answer-destroying false positives — the guard-destroys-the-answer class with four prior occurrences. C4 moved 87.9 -> 88.3, inside the instrument's own run-to-run spread (C4 read 90.0 and 87.9 on identical code 20 minutes apart), so the movement is not evidence either.
